title: EMG Recovery Authority Production IAM Principal Inventory (ADR-044/ADR-045 S4)
description: The single authoritative, declarative source of the production GCP IAM principals authorized to interact with the Recovery Authority's Spanner authority database, GCS witness bucket, and signing-domain Cloud KMS resources. Contains no project ID, billing ID, service-account email, credential, token, or private key -- only resource-pattern placeholders and permission lists. Actual provisioning of these principals against real GCP resources is out of this manifest's scope (ADR-044 §17 items 4-5; S6, not yet authorized).

id.description: Stable, unique, kebab-case principal identifier. Not a real GCP service-account email -- an environment's provisioning process maps this id to an actual identity.

domain.description: The administrative trust domain this principal belongs to (ADR-045 §4). Principals in different domains must never share IAM administration reach.

kind.description: runtime = ordinary, continuously-invoked production traffic. administrative = exceptional, governed, human-initiated-or-approved action (e.g. key rotation, compromise declaration, bootstrap).

pattern.description: A GCP resource-name PATTERN with {placeholder} segments only -- never a literal project/instance/bucket/key-ring/key ID.

required_permissions.description: The exact IAM permission strings this principal is authorized to hold. Deny-by-absence: any permission not listed here is not granted.

forbidden_permissions.description: An explicit, illustrative, machine-checked denylist proving this principal's required_permissions set does not overlap it. Not exhaustive of all GCP permissions -- exhaustive of the specific cross-domain/administrative capabilities this design depends on excluding.

implementation_status.description: grounded_in_landed_code: this permission set is derived from an actual GCP API call present in services/recovery-authority's committed Go source. boundary_only_not_yet_implemented: no production code yet exercises this principal; only its exclusion boundary relative to other principals is established.
